To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1. the thermal operator is a simple and useful tool for factorizing thermal Feynman graphs into zero temperature ones, 2. the thermal operator can be applied to any gauge theory, and 3. the thermal operator provides a simple and intuitive way to understand the structure of thermal graphs.
the finite temperature factorization of the thermal QED graphs can be achieved with a thermal operator, and that the resulting factorization is very useful.

the thermal operator can be defined in terms of a simple exponential, that the thermal operator is a gauge invariant function of the gauge field and chemical potential, and that the thermal operator relates the finite-temperature Feynman graphs to the zero-temperature Feynmann graphs with a simple exponential.

the development of a formalism for the evaluation of the finite temperature QED graphs.
the study of the effects of a chemical potential on thermal field theory.
the development of new tools for studying QED in a hot and dense medium.

our analysis is a step towards the goal of a complete understanding of the thermal properties of the QED vacuum.
the factorization of finite temperature QED graphs is a very useful and powerful tool.
the factorization works for all finite temperature graphs in QED with a chemical potential, but only for a restricted class of graphs with a chemical potential at zero temperature.

the thermal factorization is a powerful tool to study the properties of gauge theories in the presence of charge density.

the thermal photon propagator can be factorized into a thermal photon self-energy, the thermal vacuum photon propagator and the thermal vacuum photon self-energy.
